task: Decide whether named message arguments (message c.Bump(step: 2)) are a supported contract to implement or syntax to reject.
observation: Named arguments were silently accepted by moss check for both messages and ordinary user function calls (f(a: 1), including wrong and reordered labels), yet no engine supported them: Fast Debug failed with 'unsupported expression a: 10' and native lowering failed with 'missing static specialization ... from a: 10' or a rustc parse error. No canonical doc or bootstrap source_surface entry defines labelled call arguments; labels appear only for constructors, enum cases, routes, and builtin options such as sort(v, by: key).
impact: The checker was not authoritative: a program it accepted could not run in any engine, and the failure surfaced only as backend text unrelated to the source construct.
evidence: tmp/s1/fnamed.moss with old compiler: moss check ok, run --interp 'unsupported expression a: 10'
tmp/s1/msg.moss with old compiler: rustc 'expected one of ... found :' in generated root invoke

resolution.summary: Checker now rejects labelled arguments before execution with MESSAGE_NAMED_ARGUMENT_UNSUPPORTED (check_call) and CALL_NAMED_ARGUMENT_UNSUPPORTED (check_function_call); message semantics were not expanded.

suggestion: Treat every syntax shape accepted by moss check as requiring a three-engine smoke reproducer; silent acceptance of unparsed argument forms was the root cause.

task: Replace identifier-only Fast Debug FileIO reachability with semantic resolution without weakening fail-closed behaviour.
observation: The checker's retained semantic facts were not complete enough to replace identifier reachability on their own: transitive observable effects do not propagate FileIO through messages, semantic_call_edges skip on_fail arms, test bodies are walked with an empty environment, and a statement such as 'echo message a.H(), 1 + message b.H()' records an edge only for the first message. A first edge-narrowing attempt was fail-open for exactly that line until a per-line message-count guard was added.
impact: Semantic resolution could be used only as a narrowing refinement guarded by completeness checks, with identifier reachability kept as the fail-closed base; a full semantic preflight would need a complete checked call/message graph.
evidence: src/moss.cpp collect_callable_edges (handler.body only, tests with empty TypeEnv)
tmp/s1/twomsg.moss reached FileIO in Fast Debug before the message-count guard
tests/tooling/check_phase25_s1_checker_authority.py 'same-named handlers on one line, one unrecorded by the checker'

resolution.summary: Preflight narrows handler targets with checked message edges only when every message keyword on the line has a recorded target; otherwise it follows every handler of that name.

reproducer: tmp/s1/twomsg.moss (two domains with handler Flush, one reaching FileIO, both messaged on one echo line)
suggestion: Record message edges for every message expression (including nested and on_fail arms) and walk test bodies in the main composition environment so tooling can rely on semantic_call_edges as complete.
